rationale: All three review lenses converged on one major finding: the finally block in handleGateSaveAndUnpublish unconditionally clears gateError and pending refs, which closes the PublishGateFindingsModal on save-error exit paths — leaving the user unable to retry. Two minor findings were also raised: handleSkipValidation in useMissingIntegrationsModal lacks the success===false guard added to handleSubmit, and the status toast message snapshots the store state after async calls that may mutate it. Acceptance criteria 1–12 all pass on the happy path; the major finding is in the error-recovery path. The 174-file diff is full branch history from main; all 5 task-relevant files were fully reviewed.

findings.problem: The finally block calls setGateError(null) and clears pendingFormValues/pendingAssistantId unconditionally, including on the two early-return error paths (save failure and unpublish failure). This closes the PublishGateFindingsModal and wipes all recovery state on error.
findings.impact: When updateAssistant returns an error, the user sees the toast then the modal disappears. All pending state is gone — the only recovery is to re-trigger the full gate-check flow (form save → revalidation modal → gate check) from scratch.
findings.recommendation: Move setGateError(null) and the ref clears out of finally and into the success path only (after closeConfigForm() on line 164). Keep setIsSavingAndUnpublishing(false) in finally so the spinner always clears. On error exits leave gateError set so the modal stays visible and the user can retry or choose 'Keep editing'.

findings.problem: handleSkipValidation calls onSuccess() unconditionally after a non-error response, without the success===false guard that was added to handleSubmit. Currently unreachable from the gate-check flow, but any future caller whose onSubmit returns { success: false } as a non-error intercept would cause handleSkipValidation to call onSuccess() and close the form without a real save.
findings.impact: No current breakage. Future callers wiring the same sentinel pattern would silently trigger success callbacks on a paused-save scenario.
findings.recommendation: Add the same guard to handleSkipValidation after the response is received: if (response.success === false) return { success: false }.

findings.problem: The toast message is derived from selectedAssistant?.marketplace_status after the async updateAssistant call, which may have mutated the store and changed the status before the toast runs.
findings.impact: Cosmetically wrong toast text (generic 'unpublished' instead of 'removed from review queue') in a race-condition scenario. Does not affect correctness of save or unpublish.
findings.recommendation: Snapshot the status before the async calls: const statusSnapshot = selectedAssistant?.marketplace_status?.toUpperCase() at the start of the function, and use statusSnapshot in the toast logic.
